sections.skill: Plan around supplier terms and communicate delays early

questions.prompt: What is lead time?

choices.text: How long from order to delivery
The time until a loan is repaid
The time a customer spends reading an ad
The length of a business meeting

questions.correct_answer: How long from order to delivery
questions.intro: Suppliers have terms too: minimum order quantities, lead time (how long from order to delivery), payment terms, and return rules. Plan orders so supplies arrive before you need them. When something will be late, from your supplier or from you, COMMUNICATE EARLY: tell the customer what happened, the new expected date, and what you will do (for example, offer a choice to wait or cancel). Silence makes customers assume the worst; honest updates keep trust.

questions.prompt: Which message keeps trust?

choices.text: "Maybe I'll come, maybe not, we'll see"

questions.intro: If a friend is going to be 30 minutes late for dinner, a text saying "Running 30 minutes late, traffic, still coming—want to order without me?" feels fine. A friend who just never shows up and says nothing feels terrible. Businesses work the same way: a delay with an early, honest message keeps trust; silence breaks it.
